question.problem:
Consider the absolute value equation 

$$
-8|2x+1|+20=4.
$$

This equation can be expressed in the following equivalent form:

$|2x+1|=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We can rearrange the equation to isolate the absolute value on the left side:

First, we subtract $20$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-8|2x+1|+20 & =4 \\ -8|2x+1|+20-20 & =4-20 \\ -8|2x+1| & =-16\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $-8:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-8|2x+1| & =-16 \\ \frac{-8|2x+1|}{-8} & =\frac{-16}{-8} \\ \frac{\cancel{-8}|2x+1|}{\cancel{-8}} & =2 \\ |2x+1| & =2\end{aligned}
$$
